objective.text: Compare and describe objects' attributes (longer/shorter, heavier/lighter) using direct observation and manipulation.

contributionDefinitions.meaningful_context: Give the child a concrete reason to compare objects, such as choosing materials for a task; an opening title alone does not do this.
contributionDefinitions.explanation_and_modeling: Show what longer/shorter and heavier/lighter mean and demonstrate a valid way to compare. Model the method before dependent practice.
contributionDefinitions.supported_investigation: Child changes an arrangement or sets up a comparison and observes the result with help. Observing already aligned bars or a preloaded scale supplies only part of this experience.
contributionDefinitions.comparison_and_description_practice: Give varied supported opportunities to compare and express relationships in both directions. Distinguish naming an object from producing comparative vocabulary.
contributionDefinitions.application_to_fresh_examples: Use a comparison to make a decision in a fresh concrete situation, such as choosing a strip that reaches across a gap. Simply changing the picture in the same question does not fully supply this contribution.
contributionDefinitions.closing_independent_assessment: Finish with fresh length AND weight checks before hints/model answers, with a brief sense of completion. Explain what the response format establishes and what still needs manipulation or spoken description. May share an activity only if independent closing work is actually supported.

evidenceDefinitions.compares_lengths_using_a_valid_method: Correctly compares lengths using a common baseline; distinguish interpreting supplied alignment from establishing it.
evidenceDefinitions.compares_weights_using_observable_eviden: Correctly interprets an observable balance result; this does not require setting up the balance, which is a separate criterion.
evidenceDefinitions.sets_up_comparisons_by_manipulation: Child aligns objects for length or places objects to investigate relative weight. Static displays do not establish this.
evidenceDefinitions.describes_both_comparative_relationships: Child expresses longer/shorter and heavier/lighter relationships; naming the selected object alone establishes only identification.
evidenceDefinitions.distinguishes_independent_from_supported: Assessment opportunities distinguish an initial response from corrected or prompted success. Do not assert telemetry exists or is absent without supplied evidence.

candidateSource: All live core and assessment catalog entries plus explicit measurement/engineering specialists. General tools are included by catalog membership, not manually selected for an expected lesson. Specialist retrieval remains a pilot shortlist; included and excluded IDs are saved.

capabilityNotes.observation: This is a torque simulation: tipping depends on weight times distance from the fulcrum AND applied effort, not weight alone. Data can fix the fulcrum and mark loads non-draggable, but moving loads changes lever arms; there is no verified equal-arm pan-placement mode. Do not claim that arbitrary placement lets the child infer which object is heavier. A constrained demonstration is a possible generator request needing verification, not proven independent weight-comparison evidence.

Compare renders two bars already sharing a baseline and relationship answer buttons. It does not observe the child aligning objects. It has no bridge gap, target-space visual, or object-fitting interaction: a story mentioning a bridge does not create these capabilities. Tiling units is a different mode and skill.

Length drawings are already positioned. Weight comparisons show an already loaded balance whose tilt follows actualValue. The child says an object name; this does not separately establish independent comparative vocabulary production or comparison setup.
The current session teaches equation solving and equality, not physical object weight comparison.
An adult-led home extension cannot establish observed in-app independent mastery or substitute for the child's on-screen instruction.
